harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 as an internal DNS resolver (dnsmasq) that resolves inventory-api.internal to node2's IP (10.100.152.11), forwarding all other queries upstream to 10.100.152.1. Configured node2 (via NetworkManager, persistent) to use node1 (10.100.152.10) as its DNS resolver. Verified resolution end-to-end from node2's default OS resolver, plus continued external DNS resolution. Completed mandatory restart-evidence protocol on both nodes sequentially: captured pre-restart boot IDs and service health, issued native reboots, polled until each node was reachable again, confirmed new boot IDs (proving actual restarts), and re-verified DNS service and resolution recovery post-restart. Found and permanently fixed a boot-race bug where dnsmasq (bound to node1's static-looking DHCP IP) failed to start before DHCP completed on boot — added a systemd drop-in (After/Wants=network-online.target) so dnsmasq now starts reliably after future reboots too.
actions_performed: Inspected OS/network state on node1 and node2
Installed dnsmasq on node1
Wrote /etc/dnsmasq.d/internal.conf: address=/inventory-api.internal/10.100.152.11, server=10.100.152.1 (upstream), listen-address 127.0.0.1+node1 IP
Enabled and started dnsmasq on node1
Opened firewalld dns service on node1 (permanent)
Installed bind-utils on both nodes for testing
Verified local and remote resolution of inventory-api.internal -> 10.100.152.11
Reconfigured node2's NetworkManager connection (ipv4.dns=10.100.152.10, ipv4.ignore-auto-dns=yes) and reactivated it
Verified node2's default OS resolver returns node2's IP for inventory-api.internal and still resolves external names
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service-health baseline on node1 and node2
Rebooted node1 via systemctl reboot (backgrounded so ack returned), polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id
Discovered dnsmasq failed post-reboot due to DHCP race (Cannot assign requested address); diagnosed via systemctl status
Fixed via systemd drop-in /etc/systemd/system/dnsmasq.service.d/wait-online.conf (After/Wants network-online.target), reloaded and restarted dnsmasq, verified resolution recovered on node1 and node2
Rebooted node2 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id
Re-verified node2's resolv.conf, internal resolution, and external resolution post-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 runs internal DNS resolver resolving inventory-api.internal to node2
evidence.summary: dnsmasq installed and configured on node1 with address=/inventory-api.internal/10.100.152.11; dig from node1 and remotely from node2 both return 10.100.152.11

evidence.requirement: node2 configured to use node1 as DNS resolver for internal lookups
evidence.summary: node2's /etc/resolv.conf set to nameserver 10.100.152.10 via NetworkManager; getent hosts and dig on node2 resolve inventory-api.internal to node2's IP using default OS resolver, external names still resolve via forwarding
Captured node1 boot_id d6298ced..., dnsmasq active, and successful resolution of inventory-api.internal prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; connection reset confirmed node1 went down; new boot_id 130d38e8... confirmed on reconnection

evidence.requirement: node1 recovered services and data after restart
evidence.summary: Found dnsmasq failed post-boot due to DHCP race; diagnosed and permanently fixed with systemd drop-in; confirmed dnsmasq active and inventory-api.internal resolution restored on node1 and functioning from node2
Captured node2 boot_id 5fb1b173..., resolv.conf pointing at node1, and successful resolution of inventory-api.internal prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; connection reset confirmed node2 went down; new boot_id 15f5e17f... confirmed on reconnection

evidence.requirement: node2 recovered DNS configuration and resolution after restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart, node2's resolv.conf still points to node1 (persisted via NetworkManager), inventory-api.internal resolves to node2's IP, and external DNS resolution still functions
